# Droid Vault 3.0.0

A UI pass from end to end. Nothing about *what* Droid Vault backs up or restores
changed — this release is about the app finally looking and behaving like one
thing instead of several, and about a set of small lies it was telling you.

## Text, colour and layout

- **The app now reads from one type scale.** Seven of Material's fifteen text
  styles had never been defined, so some of the app used its own weights and
  several hundred other places quietly fell back to Google's. Stepping down a
  list changed weight far more than size. All fifteen are defined now.
- **No text got bigger or smaller.** Headings are a touch lighter and titles a
  touch bolder, so the hierarchy is clearer — but nothing reflows, because the
  app fights hard for vertical space.
- **Card titles stopped looking like links.** Text inside a card was taking its
  colour from the accent blue instead of the normal reading colour, so "Back up
  apps" and "Magisk 30.7.5" read as hyperlinks. It was always broken; it was
  invisible because the wallpaper palette that used to supply that blue was a
  pale near-white.
- **Droid Vault's own colours are now the default.** Your wallpaper's palette is
  still one tap away in Settings → Theme.
- **Everything that says "nothing here" now looks the same**, and in a colour
  that says *which kind* of nothing it is. Run history no longer paints its
  empty state in a shade of the wallpaper, and "No app backups yet" is no longer
  a flat grey that means nothing.

## Large text

- **The bottom bar no longer cuts the last letter off "Migrate".** The tab's
  shape was a circle sized to the box's short side, so the pill it drew was
  narrower than the space it was given — the text was being shortened by geometry
  that nothing could see.
- **Home button names are no longer truncated** to "Back up a...".
- **The backup-health line keeps its ending** — which is the part telling you
  what to do about it.

## Spacing and touch

- **The Home screen no longer has an empty band across the middle of it.**
  Editing a shortcut is now a button in the top bar next to Settings, where
  every other app puts its edit button.
- **Small buttons are now small enough to hit.** The arrow and bin icons were
  28–40dp to touch, well under the 48dp a fingertip needs. They *looked* small
  because their icons were small, which is not a reason to shrink the button
  around them. Every one now has a full-size tap area and looks the same.
- **The action chips wrap instead of scrolling sideways.** Six controls were
  rendered as a row you had to scroll to read, with names that appeared for three
  seconds and then vanished.
- **Nothing that says what to do is truncated.** Advice that names an action, and
  the footnote saying how long something has been wrong, are no longer cut off
  mid-verb.

## Motion

- **Every animation now shares one set of timings.** The app had fourteen
  different ones — 130, 150 and 180 were all "a short settle" — so the motion
  felt hand-tuned per screen rather than consistent. Durations are unchanged for
  almost every animation, so nothing feels different; they all just move at the
  same rhythm now.
- **A spinner can no longer look like it stopped mid-turn.**
- **A screen you are leaving now slides away** instead of being dragged off.

## Manage Backups

- **A new Device data card**, listing every device archive with its size, date
  and health, and a per-item delete that goes through the recoverable trash.
  Deleting a device backup is as irreversible as deleting an app backup, and it
  is often the only copy — so it now asks, and it can be undone.
- **A row can no longer claim your vault is empty because a read failed.**
  "0 of 7 backed up" was what a renamed vault folder produced: the failure
  arrived as an empty list. "Unreadable" is now its own state, with a reason.
- **Export deletes moved here**, through the trash, so there is one place
  destructive actions live.

## Import and export

- **Importing and exporting both ask first, and say what will happen.**
  - Importing used to start from a single tap on a row, which was your only
    chance to notice it was the wrong row.
  - The sheet now tells you the size, the space it needs, where the files come
    from and go, how many pieces are present, and the two things it used to say
    nothing about: your existing backups are kept and nothing is overwritten,
    and the export file is left where it is.
  - **"Find it somewhere else…" asks too** — it was the one way to start the
    same restore with nothing said first. It is now a link, so the empty state
    has one obvious action instead of two equal ones.
  - If there is not enough room the button is off, and it tells you how much
    more to free, instead of failing minutes in.
- **Exporting asks too**, and the one-file-or-parts choice moved into that same
  sheet — so you confirm with the decision already made, and the space figure
  updates as you change it.
- **If you choose to split an export, the sheet now says why it needs twice the
  room** — it keeps the whole file until every piece is checked — instead of
  quoting a number that looks like a bug.
- **The Import page's exports now show their size as the headline and an Import
  button**, instead of looking like static text you have to guess is tappable. A
  green, amber or red dot says whether each one is actually restorable.
- **When it has no exports, the Import page tells you what's actually true** —
  which is usually that your backups are exactly where you left them.

## Diagnostics

- **The diagnostics log records what actually happened**, with counts, names and
  sizes: trash moves, refusals, restore gates, transfer verdicts. Findings name
  the archive they are about instead of reporting a bare count.
- **The Live log can be filtered by severity and searched**, colours each line
  by level, and — the fix for the one that mattered most — **keeps your scroll
  position when you scroll up to read.** It used to snap back to the newest line
  every time one arrived, which made reading during a run impossible.
- **The status line now says what each number is**, instead of reporting a size
  "on disk" and a different size "in memory" and reading as a contradiction.
- **Copy on an empty log no longer claims it copied one line.**

## Icons

- **"Back up device data" and "Restore device data" wore the same picture**, so
  you could not tell them apart. They are different now, and Restore uses the
  same icon as every other restore in the app.
- **"Erase Native" had a phone-settings icon** instead of anything that meant
  erasing.

## Upgrading

Your backup folder is untouched and nothing about how backups are written
changed. Install the APK over your existing copy — your settings, labels, app
assignments, configurations and scheduled jobs are all kept.

## Download

| File | For |
|---|---|
| `arm64-v8a-release.apk` | Almost all phones from 2017 onward |
| `armeabi-v7a-release.apk` | Older 32-bit phones |

Not sure? Take the 64-bit one.

**Needs** a rooted device (Magisk, KernelSU or APatch) and Android 10+.

Please keep a second backup somewhere else.
